intro: Text Repeater takes the text you paste in and repeats it a set number of times, joining the copies with the separator you choose. It's handy for quickly generating repeated lines, filler content, or duplicated values without writing a script or a loop by hand. Pick a count, choose how the copies are separated, and the multiplied text appears instantly.
useCases: Generate placeholder or filler text by repeating a sample line many times
Create repeated rows or values for testing how an app handles bulk input
Duplicate a snippet several times separated by commas to build a quick list
Produce a block of identical lines for seeding logs, fixtures, or mock data
Repeat a string a fixed number of times when prototyping without writing code

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Text Repeater runs entirely in your browser and nothing you type is uploaded or stored remotely. The repetition happens locally on your device.

faq.q: How do I control how the copies are separated?
faq.a: Use the Separator option to join the repeated copies with a newline, a comma, a space, or nothing at all (None). Newline is the default.

faq.q: Is there a maximum repeat count?
faq.a: Yes. The count is clamped between 1 and 10,000, so very large or out-of-range values are capped to that range.

faq.q: What happens if I enter an invalid count?
faq.a: If the count field is empty or not a valid number, it falls back to 1. Decimal input is truncated to a whole number when parsed.

faq.q: Does it repeat the entire input or split it line by line?
faq.a: It repeats the whole input text as a single block, copying it the requested number of times and joining the copies with your chosen separator.
